_about: Where each sound comes from. A recording: a Wikimedia Commons file and the seconds to cut (start, end), optionally rate (below 1 slows it down and lowers it, like a slowed tape) and gain in dB. A designed sound: layers, each another sound here by name (from) or a file, with its own rate, gain and start time (at). then: a synthesized sound the page plays right after. hp, lp: high- and low-pass in Hz (hp defaults to 70). shelf: dB at 250 Hz and below; presence: dB around 1.1 kHz (deep sounds use both, so a phone speaker can play them).

neigh.note: a horse whinnying (for the zebra's neigh)

bigroar.note: T. rex: a lion's roar slowed down, an alligator's bellow under it and a low elephant trumpet

ooh.file: File:Pant-hoot call made by a male chimpanzee.ogg
ooh.note: a chimpanzee's pant-hoot, the end of the build-up and two screams (for the monkey)

bray.note: an African penguin's bray, twice: haw haw

squawk.note: a scarlet macaw squawking twice (high-passed to take out the traffic rumble behind it)

ribbit.note: a frog croaking twice: ribbit, ribbit

stego.note: stegosaurus: an alligator's rumbling grunt, slowed down (then two synthesized footsteps)

hoot.file: File:Bubo virginianus - Great Horned Owl XC450919.mp3
hoot.note: a great horned owl's hoo, hoo-hoo, hoooo, sped up half again (its real hoot is too deep for a phone speaker to play)

meow.file: File:Meow of a Siamese cat - freemaster2.wav

screech.note: a red-tailed hawk's scream, a little slower and lower (for the eagle and the pterodactyl)

peep.note: chicks peeping (for the chick and the baby dinosaur)
